newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities sues New Hampshire.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities sues New Hampshire.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Monday it is filing suit in U.S. District Court in Concord, N.H., against the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission challenging its February 28 restructuring order.

The company said it is seeking an immediate restraining order to prevent the order from becoming effective. The company is joined in the suit by three subsidiaries -- Public Service Co of New Hampshire, North Atlantic Energy Corp and Northeast Utilities Service Co.
Of immediate concern, it said, is a portion of the order that would trigger changes in the companies accounting rules.
The New Hampshire order states PS New Hampshire's stranded cost recovery level must be based on the average market price of electricity in New England, Northeast Utilities explained.

By basing rates on market prices rather than costs, the utility's auditors concluded, PS New Hampshire could no longer use regulatory accounting and would have to write off over $400 million of regulatory assets, the company continued.

It also said the order could result in violation of key provisions of some loan agreements, potentially allowing lenders to demand immediate repayment of more than $1 billion of debt. This could force loan defaults, it pointed out.

Northeast Utilities said the lawsuit also challenges portions of the order such as the enforceability of the bankruptcy court-approved 1989 rate agreement between the state and PS New Hampshire, the level of strandable assets, the forced divestiture of generation and the preemption of New Hampshire's actions by federal law.

In addition to the federal suit, Northeast Utilities said, it plans to shortly file in New Hampshire Superior court seeking from the state recovery of damages resulting from various portions of the order that the company considers a breach of contract.
"Despite all these necessary legal steps ... I still believe a fair and equitable solution to these problems can be found," NU chief executive Bernard M. Fox said.

"My hope is that we can move ahead by negotiating with the state -- even as this litigation moves forward -- so we can resolve these issues, remove the specter of a large damage claim against the state and not see massive litigation indefinitely halt electric industry restructuring in New Hampshire."
With support from the state, he added, PS New Hampshire feels it is possible to reduce rates substantially while avoiding the issues in this order that ar so problematic.
